Here's your checklist for starting your packaged drinks business in Oyo. The steps are in the order the regulators require them—you can't skip ahead because each one depends on the last.

**Start here (ready now)**

1. Make sure your product composition meets NAFDAC's Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations [1]
2. Register your business name with CAC [2]
3. Search for trademark availability [3]
4. Check whether your product needs SON MANCAP certification (optional but recommended) [4]
5. Get food handler medical tests for your production staff [1]

**Once your CAC registration comes through**

6. Set up your production facility to meet NAFDAC requirements [1]
7. Get your Federal Tax ID [5]
8. Register with Oyo State tax authority [5]
9. File your trademark application [3]
10. Apply for MANCAP if needed [4]
11. Register your business premises with Oyo State [6]

**Before you can sell**

12. Get your trademark examined and accepted [3]
13. Wait for the trademark publication and opposition period [3]
14. Apply for NAFDAC facility inspection [1]
15. Send samples for laboratory analysis [1]
16. Register your product with NAFDAC [1]
17. Get your product labels approved [1]
18. Receive your trademark registration certificate [3]

**Every year**

19. File CAC annual returns [2]
20. Renew your Oyo State business premises registration [6]
21. Renew your NAFDAC product registration [1]
22. Renew your trademark [3]

Would you like me to walk through any of these steps in detail, or shall I save this checklist so you can come back to it?

**Sources**

1. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)
2. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
3. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)
4. Product certification for locally made products — Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) MANCAP (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [son.gov.ng](https://son.gov.ng/mancapservice/)
5. Tax registration — federal (Nigeria Revenue Service) and state internal revenue services (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.nrs.gov.ng](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/)
6. State business premises permits — Oyo, Lagos, FCT, Rivers, Ogun and Edo (information as of 25 Oct 2026) · [trade.oyostate.gov.ng](https://trade.oyostate.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/PROCEDURES-FOR-REGISTRATION-OF-BUSINESS-PREMISES.pdf)

For export requirements and fees, you'll need to contact NAFDAC directly (0700-1-NAFDAC) or check with the Nigerian Export Promotion Council. I can pass you to a human adviser who may have more detail on export pathways, or you can start with the domestic registration and then ask NAFDAC what changes for export.
